03:21 - 04:03 Jared: Understood. quick note — for sub-200ms p99 you typically need local KV cache + smaller sequence lengths or quantized model variants. with Dedicated we can guarantee lower tail latency because of fixed GPU pools; with Private EU edge you get locality but there's extra ops for the network and on-prem KMS.

04:47 - 05:13 Samira: Good callout. We recommend a policy: prefer EU edge for requests from EU region; if capacity is saturated or edge unhealthy, automatically route to nearest compatible model in region-locked Dedicated capacity, with a circuit-breaker after X seconds. that behavior is configurable per route.
05:14 - 05:45 Hannah: And audit logs — are they preserved for private deployments? we need immutable logs with retention of 7 years for regulatory reasons.
05:46 - 06:20 Jared: Yes. Private comes with customer-managed logging sinks; we can push to your SIEM and enable tamper-evident logs. for Hosted we also provide audit logs but retention tiers differ, we can add long-term retention as an add-on.

07:11 - 08:00 Samira: short answer: Private has higher upfront platform fees and infra ops (especially if on-prem), Dedicated is mid-tier — committed GPU pool you own virtually, lower per-token cost than Hosted at large scale. we'll send a committed uplift worksheet showing per-token and per-hour comparisons across the three options.
08:01 - 09:05 Priya: For the EU edge pilot we only need a small footprint initially — maybe two 80GB A100-equivalent instances for a 6-week pilot. can Redwood support a pilot and also run a short latency benchmark?
09:06 - 10:00 Jared: Yes, we can provision a pilot environment. plan: provision EU edge nodes, run synthetic and capture KV cache warmup, run real traffic replay for a 72-hour window. deliverables: latency report, cost summary, and model output audit. note: the KV cache warmup is important — cold cache can double p99.
10:01 - 10:40 Evan: what's the expected time to provision the EU edge pilot?

13:36 - 14:10 Jared: Redwood runtime supports continuous batching; for high-throughput embedding workloads we recommend separate routes with larger batch windows. we can show recommended batching configs after we run the throughput projection.

15:01 - 15:38 Samira: You can pin model versions per route and include rollback policies in the rollout. We also offer quality monitoring with alert thresholds tied to your eval prompts. If there's a regression, we can auto-fallback.
15:39 - 16:20 Evan: On pricing, if we commit to 12 months for a 2x uplift, what's the discount band?
16:21 - 17:00 Samira: We'll put exact bands in the worksheet. ballpark: 15–25% off token rates for a 12-month commit at 2x baseline, plus further discounts for multi-region reserved capacity. final numbers depend on model mix and burst profile.

18:11 - 19:00 Leo (CSM): Yes, Redwood Console has token-level and route-level cost breakdowns. we'll enable a billing export to your accounting S3 bucket.

20:21 - 21:00 Samira: Yes, we'll share SOC2 attestation and recent pentest summary. for Private deployments we'll also include the network hardening checklist.
